post.summary: Sign the club in and obtain a club access/refresh token pair
post.description: Club accounts only: a player's email and password are refused with `invalid_credentials`, exactly as a stranger's are.

post.summary: Rotate the club's access and refresh tokens
Sign the club out: revoke its refresh token (idempotent)
Forgot password?: email the club a link and a code
post.description:
Sends an email with a button and an 8-character code, valid for **one hour** and usable once. The button opens the club website's own `/reset/<token>` page; the code does the same from wherever the person asked.

**Nobody can use this to learn who has an account**: the answer is `202` with no body for an address with an account, without one, and for one asked for too often. **Throttled per address** — past three emails in an hour, a request sends nothing and says so to nobody. A newer email replaces the older one's link and code.

202.description: Accepted — **the same answer whether or not the address has an account**, and whether or not an email was sent.

post.summary: Exchange the club's emailed code for a ticket
post.description:
The address and the code from the email, exchanged for a short-lived `ticket` the new password is then set with. A claim is not a use: until a password is set, the same code can be claimed again.

Only a **right** code learns why it cannot be used; a wrong one is `code_incorrect` whatever else is true.

400.description: `code_incorrect` (`details.field`: `code`) — not the code sent to that address, **or nothing was sent to it**: the two are one answer. Five wrong codes lock the credential.

409.description: The code is right, and it can no longer be used: `credential_expired` (ask again), `credential_used` or `credential_locked` (five wrong codes).

post.summary: Set the club's new password, sign out everywhere, and sign in
post.description: Sets the new password with **exactly one** of the email's link `token` or a claimed code's `ticket`, then **signs out everywhere** and signs this session in: every access token issued before this moment is refused (`access_token_revoked`) and every refresh token revoked, so another browser still signed in is signed out on its next request. The answer is this session's new token pair. The link, the code and the ticket are spent.

400.description: `password_too_weak` (`details.field`: `password`) — 8 to 128 characters with a letter and a digit. The link and the code still work.

404.description: `credential_not_found` — a link or a ticket this surface never issued.

409.description: `credential_expired` (ask again), `credential_used`, `credential_locked`, or `ticket_expired` — the code was right and the password came too late; claiming the code again is a fresh ticket.

post.summary: Sign a club up, with the account its desk signs in with
post.description: Creates the club and its account **together, in one transaction**. There is no verification step. The account then signs in at `POST /api/v1/club/auth/login` — this route issues no tokens.

400.description: A field the desk has to correct, named by `details.field` — the five details' codes, and `email_invalid` or `password_too_weak`. Every field is checked before the email is looked up.

409.description: `club_email_already_registered` — another club's account signs in with this email; `details.field` is `email`. A player holding the same address is never a conflict.

put.description: A full replacement of the five details, at any time. Saving them unchanged records nothing. **A sport one of the club's courts plays, or an official group declares, cannot be unticked**, and the refusal names the court or the group. Answers the details as recorded — names trimmed and collapsed, sports in the registry's order.

400.description: A field the desk has to correct, named by `details.field`: `club_name_invalid`, `club_district_invalid`, `club_city_invalid`, `club_sports_required` or `club_point_invalid`. Nothing was recorded. The website writes the sentence under that field.

409.description: `club_sport_has_courts` — the save unticks a sport one of the club's courts plays, switched off or not; `details.field` is `sports`, `details.sport` the sport and `details.court` the court's name (the first in the club's order). Delete the court or give it another sport first. Asked before the groups are. `club_sport_declared_by_group` — the save unticks a sport an official group at the club declares; `details.field` is `sports`, `details.sport` the sport and `details.group` the group's name (the first by name, where several play it). The group's administrator changes its sports first, or the sport stays ticked. Nothing was recorded either way.

get.summary: The club's courts, and the Raketa hours of each

post.description: A court is born **offered**, and offers nothing until its Raketa hours are painted (`PUT /raketa-hours`).

400.description: A field the desk has to correct, named by `details.field`: `court_name_invalid` or `court_sport_not_offered`. Nothing was recorded.

put.summary: Edit a court, or switch it off or on
put.description: A full replacement of the court's name, sport, roof and whether it is offered. **Switching it off is allowed whatever is booked on it** — a booked game is played as booked — and keeps its hours; a new sport is refused while a booking is ahead of it. Saving it unchanged records nothing.

404.description: `court_not_found` — no court of this club has that id; another club's is the same answer. Nothing was recorded.

409.description: `court_name_taken` — another court at the club has the name, ignoring case; or `court_has_bookings` — a new sport for a court with a booking ahead of it. Nothing was recorded.

404.description: `court_not_found` — no court of this club has that id; another club's is the same answer. Nothing was recorded.

409.description: `court_has_bookings` — a booking is ahead of this court, one in progress included. Switch it off instead. Nothing was recorded.

put.summary: Set the Raketa hours of one court or several
put.description: The same week on every court named — one court's *Save hours*, *Copy to other courts* or *All courts of a sport*. Recorded per court, only where the week moved. **Never refused over a booking or a card**: a booked game is played as booked, and the pattern is what the club offers from now on. Answers every court of the club.

404.description: `court_not_found` — no court of this club has that id; another club's is the same answer. Nothing was recorded.

get.summary: The hours the club has closed, that are not over yet

post.summary: Close hours without touching the weekly pattern
post.description: An hour, a day or a run of days, on every court or some. **Allowed over an hour with cards on it** — the cards move to another court or disappear, and nobody was charged — and refused over a booking.

400.description: A field the desk has to correct, named by `details.field`: `exception_reason_invalid` (`reason`), `exception_hours_invalid` (`hours`), `exception_days_invalid` or `exception_in_the_past` (`days`), `exception_courts_required` (`courts`). Nothing was recorded.

404.description: `court_not_found` — no court of this club has that id; another club's is the same answer. Nothing was recorded.

409.description: `court_booked_then` — a booking holds an hour it would close. `details` names the first: `court_id`, `booking_id` and `starts_at`. Cancel the booking first. Nothing was recorded.

delete.summary: Remove an exception, opening its hours again

404.description: `exception_not_found` — no exception of this club has that id; another club's is the same answer.

get.summary: What a court-hour costs, per sport the club offers

put.description: A full replacement: a sport left out is no longer priced. Money is **integer grosze**. **New prices apply to new cards only** — a card already dealt, and a game already booked, keep their price.

400.description: A row the desk has to correct — `details.field` is `prices` and `details.sport` names the row: `price_sport_not_offered`, `price_sport_repeated`, `price_out_of_range` (with `least` and `most`), `price_does_not_split` (with `seats`), `price_band_hours_invalid` or `price_bands_overlap`. Rows are read in the order sent. Nothing was recorded.

put.summary: Choose how the club works with Raketa
put.description: One way for the whole club — the setup checklist's second step. Changeable later; **the change applies to hours not yet booked**. Choosing the one it has records nothing. Answers the settings page.

get.summary: How the club works with Raketa, and its settings

put.summary: Save — the first time, confirm — the club's Raketa settings
put.description: Every setting, defaults included: **the first save confirms them**, the setup checklist's last step. A changed setting applies to games booked after the change. Pausing stops new cards on the club's courts; booked games are played as booked.

400.description: `setting_out_of_range` — `details.field` names the setting and `least` and `most` its range. Nothing was recorded.

409.description: `way_of_working_not_chosen` — which settings matter depends on the way, so it is chosen first. Nothing was recorded.

get.summary: The setup checklist, and whether the club is live
get.description: Read off everything the club has set, never stored. The Overview shows it until `live`, and then gives way.

get.summary: The club's administrators, and where each one stands

post.summary: Invite an administrator by name and email
post.description: Emails the person through the mail queue, in this request's transaction. **A new person** gets a button to the public site's `/invite/<token>` and an 8-character code, valid 72 hours; **an existing account** gets *"[Club] wants to make you an administrator"* and a button that opens the app, with no code. Inviting somebody this club removed invites them again.

400.description: A field the desk has to correct, named by `details.field`: `administrator_name_invalid` or `email_invalid`. Nothing was recorded and nothing was sent.

409.description: `administrator_already_invited` — that email is invited here, expired included: resend instead — or `administrator_already_active`. `details.field` is `email`.

post.summary: Resend an invitation: a fresh 72 hours
post.description: For somebody `INVITED` or `EXPIRED`. The email is the original's again, with a new link and code where it carries them; the older ones stop working.

404.description: `administrator_not_found` — no administrator of this club has that id: another club's, a removed one, or none.

409.description: `administrator_already_active` — there is nothing left to open.

post.description: **Only for an account that holds nothing but administrator profiles** — `can_reset_password` on the row. Clears the password, signs the account out everywhere, and puts the person back to `INVITED` with a fresh 72-hour email carrying the invitation's own link and code.

404.description: `administrator_not_found` — no administrator of this club has that id: another club's, a removed one, or none.

409.description: `administrator_also_plays` — the account also plays, and only its owner resets it, through *Forgot password?*; or `administrator_has_no_account` — nobody has set a password yet: resend instead. Nothing moved.

delete.description: The administrator profile ends: the person's next administrator request is refused with `not_an_administrator`. Their player profile and their sessions are untouched, and an invitation still in their inbox opens nothing.

404.description: `administrator_not_found` — no administrator of this club has that id: another club's, a removed one, or none.

get.summary: The club's official groups, and how much of each WhatsApp crowd arrived
get.description: *Official groups at [club]*: each one's name and monogram, who runs it — or `null`, *needs an administrator* — its players and how many are waiting, *From WhatsApp* as players of the WhatsApp group's size, and how many games it gave birth to. By name.

put.summary: Hand an official group over to one of the club's administrators
put.description: Any official group of the club, **one that needs an administrator included**, to any **active** Administrator. Only who answers changes: the link, who can join, the WhatsApp size, the players and **the requests waiting** all stay, and the new Administrator finds them. The previous one stops seeing it — and stays in it if they joined it as a player. Handing it to whoever runs it changes nothing. Answers the group's row as the table now reads it.

404.description: `group_not_found` — not an official group of this club: no such group, a player group whose home club this is, or another club's. Nothing was recorded.

409.description: `administrator_not_active` — the one chosen is not an active Administrator of this club: still invited, expired, removed, another club's, or nobody. Nothing was recorded; choose again from the Administrators table as it stands.

name.title: Name
name.description: As the club typed it: trimmed and collapsed.

status.description: `ACTIVE` once the invitation was taken up; `INVITED` until then; `EXPIRED` once its 72 hours have passed unanswered — resendable.

last_used_at.title: Last Used At
last_used_at.description: On an `ACTIVE` row: when the administrator profile was last used, **to the hour** — *today*, *this week*. `null` otherwise.

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: On an `INVITED` row, when it expires; on an `EXPIRED` row, when it did. `null` on an `ACTIVE` row.

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: The official groups this administrator runs now, by name — the row's dropdown. **Only on an `ACTIVE` row**: empty for somebody invited, expired or put back to invited by *Reset password*, whose groups read *needs an administrator* on the Groups table meanwhile.

can_reset_password.title: Can Reset Password
can_reset_password.description: Whether *Reset password* may be pressed: only for an account that holds nothing but administrator profiles. Pressing it anyway is `409 administrator_also_plays` or `administrator_has_no_account`.

AdministratorSchema.title: AdministratorSchema
AdministratorSchema.description:
One row of the club's Administrators table (``docs/adr/0184`` §1).
**Every status is derived**, and so is whether *Reset password* is drawn.

AdministratorStatus.title: AdministratorStatus
AdministratorStatus.description: What the Administrators table says of somebody, now.

BandDays.title: BandDays
BandDays.description: Which days a band prices: Monday to Friday, or Saturday and Sunday.

ClaimCodeRequest.title: ClaimCodeRequest
ClaimCodeRequest.description:
The address and the 8-character code from the email. The code is read
forgivingly — case, spaces and dashes are ignored — and its length is not
checked here: a code of the wrong length is simply not the right code, and
is told ``code_incorrect`` as every other one is. The bound is a cap on
what a request may carry, not a rule about codes.

ticket.title: Ticket
ticket.description: Present it as `ticket` when setting the new password. Good for `expires_in` seconds, and never past the code's own hour; claiming the code again replaces it.

ClaimTicketResponse.title: ClaimTicketResponse
ClaimTicketResponse.description: A correct code, exchanged for a ticket the new password is set with.

name.title: Name
name.description: Trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed, then 2–80 characters. Never unique. Refused with `club_name_invalid`.

district.title: District
district.description: As the desk writes it, 2–64 characters. `club_district_invalid`.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: The sports the club offers — at least one, `club_sports_required` otherwise. A sport ticked twice is ticked once, and the answer lists them in the registry's order.

point.description: The map pin. Off the globe is `club_point_invalid`.

ClubDetailsRequest.title: ClubDetailsRequest
ClubDetailsRequest.description:
The five details, **all of them on every save** — the club website edits
them on one page, and a save is a full replacement.

ClubDetailsResponse.title: ClubDetailsResponse
ClubDetailsResponse.description: A club as the desk sees it.

id.title: Id
id.description: The administratorship — the `id` of their row on the Administrators table, and what a handover names.

name.title: Name
name.description: **The name the club gave them**, whole — the one its Administrators table prints beside the same person.

ClubGroupAdministratorSchema.title: ClubGroupAdministratorSchema
ClubGroupAdministratorSchema.description: The Administrator running a group, as the club's own tables name them.

administrator.description: Who runs it now. **`null` while it needs an administrator** — the club removed whoever ran it, and nobody has been handed it: players read *[club] approves joins* and its requests wait, until a handover.

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: *Players*: every Group member — an Administrator who joined it as a player included. **The same number the group page shows**, whoever reads it.

waiting_count.title: Waiting Count
waiting_count.description: How many Join requests are waiting — the amber *N waiting*. `0` when nobody is.

whatsapp_size.title: Whatsapp Size
whatsapp_size.description: How many people the WhatsApp group it mirrors has — *of 48*.

whatsapp_percent.title: Whatsapp Percent
whatsapp_percent.description: *From WhatsApp*: `member_count` over `whatsapp_size`, as a whole percent rounded half up — *11 of 48 · 23%*. **Never capped**: more players than the WhatsApp group has is the real figure, *52 of 48 · 108%*, and the bar is drawn full.

games.title: Games
games.description: How many games **the group gave birth to** — never a game two of its members arranged elsewhere. No group picks a game yet, so `0`; the day one can, it counts them and means the same.

ClubGroupSchema.title: ClubGroupSchema
ClubGroupSchema.description: One row of the club's Groups table: an official group at the club.

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: **Every official group at the club**, whoever runs it or nobody, by name. A player group whose home club this is is not the club's, and is never here. Empty before an Administrator makes the first.

name.title: Name
name.description: Trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed, then 2–80 characters. Never unique. Refused with `club_name_invalid`.

district.title: District
district.description: As the desk writes it, 2–64 characters. `club_district_invalid`.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: The sports the club offers — at least one, `club_sports_required` otherwise. A sport ticked twice is ticked once, and the answer lists them in the registry's order.

point.description: The map pin. Off the globe is `club_point_invalid`.

email.title: Email
email.description: Unique among club accounts, and may also belong to an unrelated player. Malformed is `email_invalid`; another club's is `409 club_email_already_registered`.

password.title: Password
password.description: 8–128 characters with a letter and a digit — the player's rule. `password_too_weak` otherwise.

ClubSignUpRequest.title: ClubSignUpRequest
ClubSignUpRequest.description:
A club signs up: its details, and the email and password its desk signs
in with. **No second password field** — the website asks once.

name.title: Name
name.description: What the club calls it — *Court 2*, *Kort centralny*. Trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed, 1–40 characters: `court_name_invalid`. Unique among the club's courts, ignoring case: `409 court_name_taken`.

sport.description: One sport, from the club's own: `court_sport_not_offered` otherwise.

indoor.title: Indoor
indoor.description: Indoor, or outdoor. Shown on a player's card.

offered.title: Offered
offered.description: `false` switches it off: kept, with its hours, and selling nothing new. Allowed whatever is booked on it.

CourtChangeRequest.title: CourtChangeRequest
CourtChangeRequest.description:
A court's edit form: the three facts it was added with, and whether it
is offered — **all four on every save**, a full replacement.

name.title: Name
name.description: What the club calls it — *Court 2*, *Kort centralny*. Trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed, 1–40 characters: `court_name_invalid`. Unique among the club's courts, ignoring case: `409 court_name_taken`.

sport.description: One sport, from the club's own: `court_sport_not_offered` otherwise.

indoor.title: Indoor
indoor.description: Indoor, or outdoor. Shown on a player's card.

CourtRequest.title: CourtRequest
CourtRequest.description: A court as the desk types it into *Add a court* or its edit form.

offered.title: Offered
offered.description: Offered to Raketa, or switched off — kept, with its hours, and selling nothing.

hours.title: Hours
hours.description: The hours of an ordinary week this court is offered to Raketa, Monday-first and in the grid's order. Empty until they are painted.

CourtResponse.title: CourtResponse
CourtResponse.description: A court as the desk's table shows it.

courts.title: Courts
courts.description: Every court the club has, in the order they were added.

ErrorResponse.description: The body of every error response, on both API surfaces.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable identifier for this exact failure. The only half of the envelope a client may branch on.
code.title: Code

message.description: Human-readable diagnostic. Never the copy shown to a user — that is the client's, chosen from the code.
message.title: Message

trace_id.description: This request's identifier, also returned on the X-Request-ID header. Ties a client-side failure to a server log without logging a payload.
trace_id.title: Trace Id

details.description: Structured context for this code, when the code defines any.
details.title: Details

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

court_ids.title: Court Ids
court_ids.description: `null` closes **every** court, one added later included; a list closes those — at least one (`exception_courts_required`), each the club's (`404 court_not_found`).

first_day.title: First Day
first_day.description: The first local day it closes.

last_day.title: Last Day
last_day.description: The last local day it closes, inclusive — on or after `first_day` (`exception_days_invalid`), and not already over (`exception_in_the_past`).

from_hour.title: From Hour
from_hour.description: With `until_hour`, the hours it closes on each day — 9 and 12 close 09:00–12:00. Both `null` close the whole day; one alone, or hours outside 07:00–23:00, is `exception_hours_invalid`.

until_hour.title: Until Hour
until_hour.description: The hour it closes until, exclusive.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: For the club's own records, and the label its list shows. Trimmed, 1–80 characters: `exception_reason_invalid`. No player reads it.

ExceptionRequest.title: ExceptionRequest
ExceptionRequest.description:
*Add an exception*: what, when, and why.

The three forms the desk is offered are one shape: **a date** is a run of
one day, **a range** a run of several, and **hours on a date** a run of one
day with its hours — hours on a run of several close them on each day.

court_ids.title: Court Ids
court_ids.description: `null` for every court; otherwise the courts it closes, in the club's order. A deleted court leaves the list, and an exception left naming none is gone.

exceptions.title: Exceptions
exceptions.description: Every exception not over yet — its last day today or later, at the club — by its first day, then the hour it closes from (a whole day first), then the order they were added.

ForgotPasswordRequest.title: ForgotPasswordRequest
ForgotPasswordRequest.description: *Forgot password?*: the address to send a link and a code to.

administrator_id.title: Administrator Id
administrator_id.description: An **active** Administrator of the club — the `id` of an `ACTIVE` row on the Administrators table. Anybody else is `409 administrator_not_active`.

name.title: Name
name.description: Trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed, then 2–64 characters — `administrator_name_invalid` otherwise. It becomes the person's Name if they are new to Raketa.

email.title: Email
email.description: Malformed is `email_invalid`. Already invited here — expired included — is `409 administrator_already_invited`; already active here is `409 administrator_already_active`.

InviteAdministratorRequest.title: InviteAdministratorRequest
InviteAdministratorRequest.description:
*+ Add administrator*: a name and an email, and nothing else — the club
never sets, sees or handles a password or a code.

MapPointSchema.title: MapPointSchema
MapPointSchema.description: Where the club is: the pin as the desk dropped it, never rounded.

letters.title: Letters
letters.description: The first character of each of the first two words, as typed, or the first two characters of a one-word name: *my raketa group* is `mr`, *Ogrody 33 Club* is `O3`. Draw it as it comes — never change its case.

colour.title: Colour
colour.description: A colour **key** from 0 to 7, fixed for the group for ever — derived from its id, so a rename keeps it. Map it to your own palette; the backend never names a colour.

MonogramSchema.title: MonogramSchema
MonogramSchema.description:
The group's tile, **cut by the backend** so every client draws the same
one (``docs/adr/0183`` §5).

NewPasswordRequest.title: NewPasswordRequest
NewPasswordRequest.description:
The new password, and **exactly one** of what opens the way to it: the
`token` from the email's link, or the `ticket` a claimed code returned.

The password carries no bound here, deliberately: the rule every account
shares — 8 to 128 characters with a letter and a digit — is refused as
`password_too_weak` naming the field, not as a validation error naming none.
Sending both or neither of `token` and `ticket` is a malformed request rather
than a person's mistake, and is the one refusal here that is a `422`.

offered.title: Offered
offered.description: *Offer our groups other clubs' courts when ours are full*. Off by default.

within_km.title: Within Km
within_km.description: How far such a court may be, in kilometres — kept while off.

days.description: Monday to Friday, or Saturday and Sunday.

from_hour.title: From Hour
from_hour.description: With `until_hour`, the hours it prices — 17 and 22 price 17:00–22:00. Within 07:00–23:00, at least one hour: `price_band_hours_invalid`. Two bands of the same days may not overlap: `price_bands_overlap`.

until_hour.title: Until Hour
until_hour.description: The hour it prices until, exclusive.

price_grosze.title: Price Grosze
price_grosze.description: The court-hour's price in those hours, in grosze.

share_grosze.title: Share Grosze
share_grosze.description: What one player pays of it: the price divided by the seats.

PricesRequest.title: PricesRequest
PricesRequest.description:
The whole price table, **a full replacement**: a sport left out is no
longer priced.

prices.title: Prices
prices.description: Every sport the club offers, in the registry's order, priced or not. **New prices apply to new cards only**: a card already dealt keeps the price it was dealt with.

court_ids.title: Court Ids
court_ids.description: Each court to give this week. One the club does not have refuses the whole save with `404 court_not_found`. A court named twice is named once.

hours.title: Hours
hours.description: The week, as the player's grid spells it. **Empty is allowed**: a court offering nothing. A cell sent twice is one cell.

RaketaHoursRequest.title: RaketaHoursRequest
RaketaHoursRequest.description:
*Weekly hours for Raketa*, saved on one court or several at once —
which is what *Copy to other courts* and *All courts of a sport* send.

release_lead_days.title: Release Lead Days
release_lead_days.description: Only Raketa: days before a game unsold hours return to the club. 1–13, default 3.

cut_off_hours.title: Cut Off Hours
cut_off_hours.description: Hours before a game players may leave free, and a game still short is called off. 0–72, default 24.

minimum_notice_hours.title: Minimum Notice Hours
minimum_notice_hours.description: Instant and On request: the latest a Raketa game can book, in hours before it. 1–48, default 2.

time_to_confirm_minutes.title: Time To Confirm Minutes
time_to_confirm_minutes.description: On request: minutes the club has to answer a full game. 5–60, default 30 — never more than the shortest minimum notice.

check_in.title: Check In
check_in.description: *We check players in*. Off by default.

paused.title: Paused
paused.description: *Pause Raketa bookings*: no new cards on the club's courts; booked games are played as booked, and cards already dealt keep their court until their book-by.

RaketaSettingsRequest.title: RaketaSettingsRequest
RaketaSettingsRequest.description:
The settings form — every field on every save, defaults included, since
the first save is the club **confirming** them. Each number is bounded by
the domain: `setting_out_of_range` names the field and carries `least` and
`most`.

RaketaSettingsResponse.title: RaketaSettingsResponse
RaketaSettingsResponse.description:
How the club works with Raketa, and every setting — **at its default
until the club confirms it**, so the form can show what it would save.

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: The five, in the Overview's order: `CONNECT_PAYMENTS` — `PENDING` until connecting Stripe is built — then `WAY_OF_WORKING`, `COURTS` (an offered court), `HOURS_AND_PRICES` (an offered court with hours, and every such court's sport priced) and `SETTINGS` (confirmed).

live.title: Live
live.description: Every step but a pending one is done: the club's courts can reach players' decks. A paused club is still live.

SetupResponse.title: SetupResponse
SetupResponse.description: The Overview's checklist, shown until the club is live.

SetupStep.title: SetupStep
SetupStep.description: The five steps, in the order the Overview lists them.

state.description: `DONE`, `TO_DO`, `LOCKED` — waiting on the step it needs: hours and prices on a court, the settings on a way of working — or `PENDING`: nothing the club can do yet. *Next* is the first `TO_DO`.

Sport.title: Sport
Sport.description: The four sports Raketa rates, as a closed enum.

sport.description: A sport the club offers (`price_sport_not_offered`), once per save (`price_sport_repeated`).

price_grosze.title: Price Grosze
price_grosze.description: The standard court-hour, in grosze — 12000 is 120 zł. Between `least` and `most` (`price_out_of_range`, which carries both), and splitting into whole grosze among the sport's seats (`price_does_not_split`, which carries `seats`) — so is every band's.

bands.title: Bands
bands.description: Optional hours priced differently. Empty is none.

seats.title: Seats
seats.description: How many players a game of this sport seats.

price_grosze.title: Price Grosze
price_grosze.description: The standard court-hour in grosze, or `null` — not priced yet.

share_grosze.title: Share Grosze
share_grosze.description: What one player pays of the standard price — the price divided by the seats, exact to the grosz. `null` beside a `null` price.

bands.title: Bands
bands.description: Weekdays first, then by the hour each opens.

WayOfWorking.title: WayOfWorking
WayOfWorking.description: How a club sells through Raketa (the mechanics §16.3).

way_of_working.description: `ONLY_RAKETA` — Raketa sells the club's Raketa hours alone, until the release lead; `INSTANT` — both sell and a Raketa booking is final; `ON_REQUEST` — the club confirms each full game within its time to confirm, and nobody pays until it does.

day.title: Day
day.description: ISO weekday — 1 is Monday, 7 is Sunday. The grid is Monday-first.

hour.title: Hour
hour.description: The hour the cell starts at, wall clock — 19 is 19:00 to 20:00. The week runs 07:00 to 23:00, so the first cell is 7 and the last is 22.

WeeklyHourResource.title: WeeklyHourResource
WeeklyHourResource.description:
One ticked hour of the week — a day, and the hour its cell starts at.

Two named fields rather than the single joined code the event stream stores.
The stream's code is a *storage* encoding chosen so a replay folds strings;
this is a contract a client renders a grid from, and a client that had to
split ``"3:19"`` would be parsing our persistence format.

**Every cell, and there is no exception.** The rule was twice read as
covering only the cells a player *chose* — the one a times rung offers
(#283), and the week a raised ``KEEP_THESE_TIMES`` quotes back (#286) — on
the argument that a payload handed back is not a resource. Both crossed as
codes, and in both cases a client ended up splitting one. What decides this
is not whose value it is but **what is done with it**: a cell that gets
drawn on the seven-by-sixteen grid crosses in these two fields, and the engine
holding it as a code is a fact about the engine. This side of the boundary
owns the encoding, so this side is where it is read.
